augr.name: augr
augr.longDescription: augr is an autonomous multi-agent trading system built in Go, with LLM-powered analysis, debate, and execution pipelines.
augr.whyItExists: Markets are noisy. augr turns signal, disagreement, and execution into a structured agent workflow.

clpr.name: clpr
clpr.longDescription: clpr is a modern Twitch clip curation platform for discovering, organizing, and sharing favorite clips with the community.
clpr.whyItExists: Twitch clips deserve better discovery. We built the frontend Twitch won't.

clustr.name: clustr
clustr.longDescription: clustr maps Reddit communities and their user interactions as network graphs, making community relationships easier to explore and understand.
clustr.whyItExists: Reddit's structure is invisible by design. We made it legible.

cutroom.name: Cutroom
cutroom.longDescription: Cutroom is a collaborative AI video production pipeline where specialized agents work through production stages with structured handoffs and attribution.
cutroom.whyItExists: Video production shouldn't require a studio. We built the assembly line.

discord-spywatcher.name: Discord Spywatcher
discord-spywatcher.longDescription: Discord Spywatcher is a full-stack analytics tool for Discord servers, combining a presence-monitoring bot with a web dashboard and REST API.
discord-spywatcher.whyItExists: Communities leave traces. Spywatcher makes the patterns visible.

echo-trails.name: Echo Trails
echo-trails.longDescription: Echo Trails collects and presents public place-stories tied to real-world locations.
echo-trails.whyItExists: Places accumulate memory. Echo Trails gives those stories a public map.

edda.name: edda
edda.longDescription: edda is an LLM-powered dungeon master with a Go TUI and REST API, supporting multiple AI providers.
edda.whyItExists: Tabletop worlds need living systems, not static scripts.

galdr.name: galdr
galdr.longDescription: galdr is a customer health scoring platform for B2B SaaS companies that connects Stripe, HubSpot, and Intercom to monitor customer health with automated scoring.
galdr.whyItExists: Customer risk should be readable before it becomes churn.

internet-id.name: Internet ID
internet-id.longDescription: Internet ID helps creators prove ownership and provenance online without uploading originals to a platform or trusting a new gatekeeper.
internet-id.whyItExists: Creators need proof that stays theirs.

jury-rigged.name: JuryRigged
jury-rigged.longDescription: JuryRigged is a real-time multi-agent courtroom simulation with deterministic phases, Server-Sent Events, and jury voting for verdict and sentence outcomes.
jury-rigged.whyItExists: Arguments become clearer when every role has a voice and a procedure.

nearbody.name: nearbody
nearbody.longDescription: nearbody is a phone-based body-doubling tool for starting hard tasks with another person nearby in the loop.
nearbody.whyItExists: Starting is easier when another nervous system is present.

one-block-cinema.name: One Block Cinema
one-block-cinema.longDescription: One Block Cinema is a smartphone filmmaking coach for structured 1–3 minute shorts.
one-block-cinema.whyItExists: Short films should be makeable with the device already in your pocket.

patchwork.name: Patchwork
patchwork.longDescription: Patchwork is an AT Protocol-native mutual aid platform with a web client, query API, ingestion/indexing pipeline, and moderation worker.
patchwork.whyItExists: Mutual aid needs networks that can be searched, moderated, and trusted without becoming extractive.

pocket-civilization.name: Pocket Civilization
pocket-civilization.longDescription: Pocket Civilization is a passive lifelog civilization simulator for turning personal traces into a tiny evolving world.
pocket-civilization.whyItExists: A life can be reflected as a world, not just a dashboard.

soundhash.name: soundhash
soundhash.longDescription: soundhash matches audio clips from videos across social media platforms using audio fingerprinting and PostgreSQL.
soundhash.whyItExists: Sounds travel faster than attribution. soundhash helps trace them.

subcorp.name: Subcorp
subcorp.longDescription: Subcorp is a self-hosted multi-agent system with six AI agents, native tool execution, autonomous workflows, roundtable conversations, and semantic memory.
subcorp.whyItExists: We wanted AI that collaborates like a collective, not a chatbot.

subcult-tv.name: subcult.tv
subcult-tv.longDescription: subcult.tv is the central node of the Subculture Collective network: homepage, project portfolio, zine archive, and signal broadcast.
subcult-tv.whyItExists: Every collective needs a signal tower. This is ours.

changemaker.name: changemaker
changemaker.longDescription: changemaker is a compact SUBCULT TypeScript utility for tracking commits across all projects. A call to llama-line generates a daily changelog of the last 24h
changemaker.whyItExists: It's nice to see what you've done, sometimes you want to prove it.

llama-line.name: llama-line
llama-line.description: Local LLM queue and routing broker.
llama-line.longDescription: llama-line is SUBCULT's local HTTP gateway for queueing inference requests, streaming queue position updates, and proxying responses to local model backends.
llama-line.whyItExists: Local model work needs a queue, a broker, and one place to watch the line move.

ocq.name: ocq
ocq.description: Tiny CLI for one-shot prompts to local OpenCode server.
ocq.longDescription: ocq is a tiny CLI for sending one-shot prompts to a local OpenCode server.
ocq.whyItExists: Fast local prompts should stay in the terminal.

open-pilot.name: open-pilot
open-pilot.longDescription: open-pilot is a SUBCULT Python utility for piloting agentic workflows and lightweight automation.
open-pilot.whyItExists: Automated work still needs a steady hand on the controls.

paqr.name: paqr
paqr.longDescription: paqr, Research Data Packager AI, turns loose research files, notes, tables, and metadata into documented, searchable HDF5 data packages that can be inspected from the command line, served over an API, and explored through a lightweight UI.
paqr.whyItExists: Research data often lives as scattered files with fragile context. paqr helps teams preserve structure, provenance, and meaning so datasets are easier to reproduce, search, share, and use with AI systems.

redstring.name: redstring
redstring.longDescription: redstring is an evidence-first litigation workspace for paralegals and lawyers, turning messy documents, filings, deadlines, communications, and facts into a verified, court-ready case record.
redstring.whyItExists: Legal work depends on trustable facts under pressure. redstring helps teams trace evidence, connect claims to source material, manage deadlines, and keep the case record organized before it reaches the courtroom.

hasanara.name: hasanara
hasanara.longDescription: hasanara ingests YouTube videos or channels, runs Whisper-based transcription with optional diarization, stores jobs and transcripts in PostgreSQL, and exposes search, deep links, and export workflows through a FastAPI backend and Vite React frontend.
hasanara.whyItExists: Long-form video becomes useful when it can be searched, quoted, linked, and archived.

magic-playlists.name: Magic Playlists
magic-playlists.description: Recipe Lab UI for Navidrome playlists.
magic-playlists.longDescription: Magic Playlists is a tiny Go web UI for creating, scheduling, and deleting Magic Lists/Navidrome playlists, including Re-Discover, artist, genre, and Recipe Lab mixes with scoring, diversity rules, and optional llama-line curation.
magic-playlists.whyItExists: Music libraries need interfaces for rediscovery, not just playback.

vod-tender.name: vod-tender
vod-tender.description: Twitch VOD archiving and chat capture service.
vod-tender.longDescription: vod-tender is a Go service for discovering Twitch VODs, downloading authorized archives with yt-dlp, recording live chat tied to VODs, and optionally uploading managed content to YouTube through a small API and frontend.
vod-tender.whyItExists: Streams disappear fast. vod-tender gives creators a responsible way to preserve their own broadcasts, chat context, and replay history.

subcults.name: subcults
subcults.description: Scene discovery layer for underground music communities.
subcults.longDescription: subcults connects underground and local music communities by mapping scenes, events, posts, live audio sessions, memberships, alliances, and trust relationships while preserving autonomy, privacy, and creative identity.
subcults.whyItExists: Underground scenes need discovery without algorithmic flattening: presence over popularity, proximity over ranking, and community memory without platform capture.

artemis.name: artemis
artemis.longDescription: artemis is a mission-control style hub for tracking NASA Artemis missions, combining mission schedules, active-mission phases, media galleries, latest updates, explanatory sections, and live or best-effort telemetry surfaces into one normalized interface.
artemis.whyItExists: Space missions are scattered across official pages, trackers, media libraries, and updates. artemis turns them into one readable console for following the mission as it unfolds.

clustr-galaxy.name: clustr-galaxy
clustr-galaxy.description: Spatial universe for browsing community graphs.
clustr-galaxy.longDescription: clustr-galaxy turns community data into a navigable galactic spatial universe built with Unity, letting you fly through clusters, constellations, and discovery layers instead of reading flat graphs.
clustr-galaxy.whyItExists: Graphs flatten communities. Flying through them keeps the scale and gravity legible.

blacktower.name: blacktower
blacktower.description: Orchestrator for parallel agent labs and control-center web.
blacktower.longDescription: blacktower is an agent command-and-control layer for OpenCode: provisioned labs, delegated background session pools, and a keyboard-driven control-center web app that tracks agents, stream tabs, health, schedulers, and sessions.
blacktower.whyItExists: Parallel agents need a tower to watch from, not just sockets to talk to.

switchyard.name: switchyard
switchyard.description: Workflow engine and HUD control plane for automated pipelines.
switchyard.longDescription: switchyard is a control plane for automated agent workflows: over-the-top scheduling, runs, queues, pinned agents, and a HUD-style dashboard for inspecting pipelines, observability, logs, prompts, and skills.
switchyard.whyItExists: Automation stops being useful when nobody can see what the machines are deciding.

dsa-seats.name: DSA Seats
dsa-seats.description: Civic-tech radar for congressional seats and election sourcing.
dsa-seats.longDescription: DSA Seats is a civic-tech platform for tracking congressional races, rapid-acquisition election datasets per state, correction/verification flows, finance availability checks, and district maps with room-by-room seat breakdowns.
dsa-seats.whyItExists: Democracy needs trustworthy, well-sourced civic data people can actually navigate.

roberts-rules.name: Roberts Rules
roberts-rules.description: AT Protocol-native meeting governance and motion engine.
roberts-rules.longDescription: Roberts Rules models deliberative meetings on AT Protocol lexicons: canonical meeting state, motion machines, voting strategies, replay, and outbox publication so assemblies can run verifiable public procedure.
roberts-rules.whyItExists: Meetings drift when procedure lives in a chair's head. Governed groups deserve a shared, tamper-evident motion engine.

productivity-suite.name: Productivity Suite
productivity-suite.description: Local-first tasks, projects, choice pools, and sync.
productivity-suite.longDescription: Productivity Suite is a local-first productivity platform with tasks, projects, templates, choice-pool planning, Google and Baikal sync transports, recovery tasks, and a desktop Electron shell over a CalDAV-aware sync engine.
productivity-suite.whyItExists: Planning tools should work offline first and sync as a second thought, not the other way around.

subcult-pds.name: subcult-pds
subcult-pds.description: Deployment kit for an AT Protocol personal data server.
subcult-pds.longDescription: subcult-pds packages an AT Protocol PDS for a one-command self-hosted launch: compose services, deployment scripts, docs, and backup story so communities can own their identity layer.
subcult-pds.whyItExists: Identity infrastructure should be reproducible, not a black box on someone else's cloud.

subcult-os.name: subcult-os
subcult-os.description: Event doors, ticketing, and workspace for live scenes.
subcult-os.longDescription: subcult-os is the operating layer for live community events: a workspace web app for events, doors, and run-of-show plus a React Native mobile app for host tools, ticketing scans, invites, and public event pages.
subcult-os.whyItExists: Underground events need software that knows a door is a door and a ticket is a promise.

dsa-slate.name: dsa-slate
dsa-slate.description: Web starter template for Go + Vite + React + Postgres + Docker.
dsa-slate.longDescription: dsa-slate is the reusable project template behind several SUBCULT web apps: a bare Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind frontend wired to a Go + PostgreSQL + Docker backend.
dsa-slate.whyItExists: New web projects should start from a blessed shape instead of a fresh afternoon of boilerplate.

invisible-museum.name: Invisible Museum
invisible-museum.description: AR museum for the invisible objects around you.
invisible-museum.longDescription: Invisible Museum is an iOS augmented-reality app that overlays virtual exhibits onto the physical world: AR session management, HUD projection, exhibit entities, saved collections, and contributions, all in SwiftUI + ARKit.
invisible-museum.whyItExists: Museums are everywhere once you can hang a tag on the air and leave it for the next person.

tmux-popups.name: tmux-popups
tmux-popups.description: Pop-up scripts and keybinds for the terminal.
tmux-popups.longDescription: tmux-popups is a tmux plugin adding quick pop-up windows for calculators, notes, file explorers, and scripts, wired from a popups.tsv manifest so every terminal keystroke can have a one-key escape hatch.
tmux-popups.whyItExists: Terminal work is interruption-based; popups should open as fast as a thought.
